title: Charles Street Terminal redevelopment and zero carbon building standard
subtitle: Also: road assumption policy, Ottawa Street tax grant, older adult transit pilots, regional forests, e-scooters
overview: The Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee recommended that the Region proceed with a multi-phased plan to redevelop the Charles Street Terminal in downtown Kitchener. Staff will report back on options to retain public ownership of all or part of the site and on an affordable or non-market housing framework. Staff expect a provincial record of site condition near the end of 2026, so a procurement process is realistically a 2027 matter.

The committee also recommended replacing the LEED Silver standard with the Zero Carbon Building – Design standard for new Regional facilities. This is subject to project feasibility and approved budgets, and it supports the Region's 2050 net zero target. It recommended a joint tax increment grant for 161 Ottawa Street South and an updated Regional Road Assumption Criteria Policy, both on the consent agenda.

Committee members heard staff reports on the Region's climate action plan, forests, a two-ride fare card pilot and a free day pass pilot for older adults. These were received for information. The committee heard delegations on energy, e-scooters, pedestrian safety, age-friendly transit and the terminal site. These recommendations go to Council for a final decision.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended proceeding with the multi-phased redevelopment plan and asked staff to report on options to retain public land ownership and on an affordable or non-market housing framework {{vote:m5}}.

decisions.item: Zero carbon standard for Regional facilities
decisions.detail: The committee recommended targeting the Zero Carbon Building – Design standard for new Regional facilities in place of LEED Silver, subject to feasibility and approved capital budgets {{vote:m7}}.

decisions.item: Tax increment grant, 161 Ottawa Street South
decisions.detail: As part of the consent agenda, the committee recommended a joint Tax Increment Grant not to exceed $114,580, financed from incremental tax revenue after remediation, redevelopment and reassessment.
As part of the consent agenda, the committee recommended adopting the revised and updated Regional Road Assumption Criteria Policy.

debate: On the Charles Street Terminal, councillors broadly supported phasing as a way to manage market risk, and one noted lessons from the transit hub. Several asked how green space and placemaking would be kept across multiple owners. Staff said core principles would guide each procurement and return to Council.

On public ownership, one councillor worried that raising it could deter private developers. Staff said retaining title can complicate financing for some uses but may work for others, and that the report would weigh the pros and cons. Another councillor noted that requesting public space in developments is common.

A delegate from a non-profit group urged that the terminal site stay a public, civic space with non-profit services. Another councillor wanted to see a clearer phasing picture sooner. Staff cited the delay from environmental work and the record of site condition.

On the zero carbon standard, staff said LEED Silver can be achieved without energy or carbon gains. They estimated a capital cost premium of 0 to 7% that operating savings often offset. Staff said projects already under construction would get quick wins within approved budgets rather than higher costs.

On the older adults free day pass pilot, delegates and councillors raised concerns that the app-only approach and in-person age verification exclude some seniors. One councillor proposed a hybrid, lower-barrier option. Staff said they could not commit to the July 1 start if the design changed and noted an estimated one in five people cannot take part. Other councillors urged starting the pilot and learning from it.
